subject.title: feat(gateway): idempotent start, non-interactive stop guard, unified lifecycle audit

question: Should non-interactive `gateway stop` become fail-closed by default, requiring existing automation to pass `--force`?
rationale: This is an intentional public CLI behavior change that can stop established automation from performing Gateway recovery; tests cannot choose the acceptable compatibility and operator-safety tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt the fail-closed default
options.body: Approve `--force` as the explicit non-interactive consent mechanism after supported automation callers and upgrade guidance are covered.

options.title: Preserve existing automation behavior
options.body: Keep non-interactive stop behavior compatible by making the stricter guard opt-in or otherwise limiting it to newly introduced automation paths.

recommendation.title: Adopt the fail-closed default
recommendation.body: Approve `--force` as the explicit non-interactive consent mechanism after supported automation callers and upgrade guidance are covered.

likelyOwner.reason: The assigned author owns the proposed lifecycle-policy direction and its current implementation.
